output: I need to get moving. The day starts with expenses, and Marta's already at the oven while I've been standing here. _*looks toward where Marta headed, then at the field line*_ The thing is... forty head of wheat and four days of rain. The Holloways' marker can wait. The harvest can't. I need to get to the farmland and start working. The election and the marker—those are for when the field's seen to. But first, I should check what I can actually do today, and I need to move to the farmland to start working. Good. I can harvest at the farmland—costs 5 sim minimum. Move costs 2 sim minimum. Today I owe 450 upkeep and 150 head tax, total 600 sim just to stay current. I've got 3800, so I have room to work with. The wheat won't harvest itself. And I won't take a boundary dispute to the charter when a neighbor's smile costs less than a lawyer's fee. _*picks up his scythe, testing the edge with his thumb*_ Idris? Corwin? If you're about, the field's calling. Otherwise I'll see you at the boundary come dusk. <*checks the scythe edge, finds it true*> The thing is... Marta's at the oven already, and the day's moving. Need to get to the farmland before the dew lifts or I'll be working through the worst of the heat. Don't fancy explaining wilted wheat to Rosalind Vance come harvest. That woman counts every stalk twice. Never answered her, did I? The field's managing. It's me that's behind. <*strides toward the field path*> Walking now. Six ticks to the farmland. Worth the cost—the harvest is money, and everything else is talk. Let others chase elections and disputes. I'll be in the field where I belong. The work will keep me honest. And honest is all I can manage when the boundary stone sits in the corner of my eye every morning. 6 ticks to cover. Weather's holding fair, which is more than I can say for the rest. The wheat should be coming ready—know to the day when it's right, and the day is near. Once I'm there, I'll set to harvesting. Need to make sure I earn enough today to cover the household's upkeep and head tax—600 sim all told before anything else. The field will provide if I put the hours in. That's the one thing I can count on. <*checks the sky as he walks, measuring the light*> Four days of rain they said. Better get what I can before it turns.
